answer: MPC-based proof of personhood lets a group of validators jointly verify that an applicant is human without any validator learning the applicant's biometrics, and the onyx of the design is that the biometric match is computed on secret-shared data. The terrace of the protocol is that the result is a single bit, unique or not, so no validator learns why an applicant failed. A Sybil cannot replay another person's proof because the match is bound to fresh liveness data, and the tide of the sharing keeps the biometric private forever.
